diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $(X,|\cdot|_X),(Y,|\cdot|_Y)$ be  Banach spaces  with the Approximation Property, i.e. we are given $\left\{{\mathcal S}^X_\alpha\right\}_{\alpha \in A }\subset \mathcal L(X)$, $\left\{{\mathcal S}^Y_\beta\right\}_{\beta \in B }\subset \mathcal L(Y)$ satisfying Assumption \ref{ass:approx_pro}.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the compact-open universal approximation theorem is achieved via EDAs under only AP on $X$. However, the theorem's surrounding assumptions require both $X$ and $Y$ to have the Approximation Property, and the proof explicitly uses the net ${\mathcal S}^Y_\beta$ to approximate values in $Y$. Thus the result as established by the source requires AP on $Y$ as well; the claim of 'only AP on $X$' is an unsupported scope overstatement.

failure_location.quote: via EDAs under only AP on $X$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the prose to require AP on both $X$ and $Y$, or supply a new proof that avoids ${\mathcal S}^Y_\beta$ and establishes the result with only AP on $X$.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised generality of the compact-open UAT is overstated. The paper does not establish the result under only AP on $X$.
issues.title: Overstated compact-open UAT scope: only AP on X
issues.why_classification: The formal theorem as contextualized remains valid with the additional AP on $Y$; a short prose correction preserves all substantive claims.
